answer: Temperature and humidity together fix a dew point that only real air at a real place can produce. The device reports both, the verifier checks the pair against the regional dew-point field, and mismatched pairs are rejected, so a night bright with a comet, a valley from a fable and a roof of copper each yield a distinct coupled reading. A farm reusing one sensor's numbers across accounts fails because the same dew point cannot plausibly sit in all three climates at once.
